newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-FALDO'S LONG TRIP LOOKS WORTHWHILE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FALDO'S LONG TRIP LOOKS WORTHWHILE.

text.p: Nick Faldo's long trip for Ryder Cup qualifying points looks like paying off at the British PGA Championship.

Whether he was asked by European captain Seve Ballesteros to try to qualify of whether he was stung by the Spaniard's policy of no guarantee of selection, Faldo has delivered the goods so far this weekend.
With one round to go at Wentworth, he holds a share of third place two shots behind pacesetter Ian Woosnam.
At stake on Monday is a first prize of 183,340 pounds.
Faldo currently holds 62nd place in the Cup standings with a meagre earnings of 44,905 points since qualification began last September.
He failed to improve his total when he missed the halfway cut at last month's U.S. Masters and that is when he decided to come here.
"As I didn't win too many points there, it seemed to be a fair trade," he said.
If he were to win the title on Monday -- for a record fifth time -- the prize money could vault him up to 10th place in the standings, depending on what others around that position do.
And even if he doesn't, Faldo, the hero of the 1995 victory over the Americans at Oak Hill in Rochester, New York, should pick up enough to boost his position considerably.
And he will still have enough other chances to qualify by right.
Faldo won the Nissan Open at the Riviera Club in California early in March. "That has certainly given me an indication that my game is not too shabby," he said.
But his putting went off at Augusta and he is still struggling with it despite his success at Wentworth so far this weekend.

He did not seemed perturbed by Ballesteros's threat last week that he would have "no friends" when it came time to making his two selections to add to the 10 who qualify automatically for the September rematch and that Faldo had no guarantee of being selected just on past form.
"He's all right," Faldo said of his captain. "We know what is going on. Seve says that what is driving him mad it too many questions. There is too much talk."
Even if he falters on Monday, Faldo will have ample opportunities to boost his total.
Next month's U.S. Open counts and he will play the lucrative Irish Open, the Loch Lomond Invitational and the British Open at Troon in successive weeks in July.
Then he also has the U.S. PGA championship in August before qualification ends on August 31.
With his commitments to play a required number of events on the U.S. Tour, Faldo feels he is doing all he can to meet his Ryder Cup commitment.
"I'm doing the best I can in the limited number of events I'm going to play. I cannot do any more," he said.
